newsitem.title: FRANCE: Saab wants to join Airbus - paper.
newsitem.headline: Saab wants to join Airbus - paper.

text.p: Swedish industrial group Saab AB wants to join the Airbus consortium to participate in the future A3XX, Saab chairman Bengt Halse told the Les Echos financial daily in an interview.
"For political, financial and technical reasons Europe has to bundle its forces and include Saab and Alenia which are outside the consortium," Halse said.

"We encounter a positive attitude with the consortium members. The future large carrier A3XX is the most important project for Airbus for a long time," he said, adding Saab's participation in Airbus would be limited to this plane.
"You cannot rule out anything for ever. The commercial perspectives have to be the basis for our considerations, more so than technical aspects," he said.
Airbus senior vice president John Leary told the Wall Street Journal that the 550-seat A3XX superjumbo would be priced at $198 million and that delivery could start by 2003.
The plane aims to take away business from Boeing Co for new versions of its 747 jumbo jet.
